scope: Post-freeze public-release review findings for Manager 4.17.11

defects.title: Manage Hubs disables target-driven recovery switching when active selection is unresolved
defects.preconditions: The multi-Hub registry is structurally valid and contains at least one healthy registered target, while active_instance.json is missing, corrupt, or names an instance that does not resolve.
defects.bad_behavior: The interactive Manage Hubs path reports that switching is disabled and exposes only Back, even though the runtime switch operation is intentionally target-driven and can recover by validating a healthy requested registered target without requiring the broken previous active selection.
defects.root_cause: The frontend uses successful resolution of the current active selection as a prerequisite for entering the switch UI, coupling recovery reachability to the state that recovery is intended to replace.

defects.title: Risk context accepts empty or non-ancestor base/head ranges and can false-pass pre-freeze selection
defects.defect_class: qualification range identity / fail-open risk selection
defects.preconditions: The manually dispatched Risk Defect Gate receives a base/head pair that resolves as commits but is equal, reversed, or unrelated rather than a non-empty proper-ancestor range.
defects.bad_behavior: The workflow and Build-ManagerRiskContext resolve both commits without proving ancestry. In the base=head case the diff is empty, no risk surfaces or regressions are selected, and the gate can report PASS/freeze permission when no global release blocker is otherwise open.
defects.root_cause: Diff-driven qualification trusted caller-supplied commit identities without an explicit fail-closed proper-ancestor and non-empty-range precondition.
